issues.title: test(vn-holidays): add tests/holidays.test.ts with edge cases beyond the golden fixtures
issues.body:
## Problem
`vn-holidays` has only `tests/holidays-golden.test.ts` (4 `it` blocks that iterate `tests/golden/vn-holidays.json`). Every other skill has a dedicated `tests/<name>.test.ts`, and CONTRIBUTING requires one. Behaviour that is not a pure input->output case is untested: error results for malformed dates, `announced: false` for years without data, `addWorkingDays` with n=0 or a negative n, and ranges that cross a year boundary.

## Acceptance
- [ ] New `tests/holidays.test.ts` with >= 20 cases covering: invalid date input (`ok: false` with code and hint), a year with no announcement (`announced: false`, statutory days only), weekend-collision compensation, `addWorkingDays` with n = 0 and with a negative n, and a year-boundary crossing
- [ ] Only assert behaviour the current implementation already has. If a case exposes a bug, report it in the PR instead of silently changing behaviour
- [ ] Do not edit `packages/core/data/*.json`
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: The holidays skill has no dedicated test file, unlike the other skills, and CONTRIBUTING requires >= 20 tests per skill.
issues.summary: Added tests/holidays.test.ts with 33 characterization tests (invalid input, unannounced year, weekend compensation, addWorkingDays n=0/negative, year boundary). No behaviour changes; no bugs found.

Closes #60

Adds `tests/holidays.test.ts` with 33 characterization tests for `vn-holidays`. Before this, the skill only had `tests/holidays-golden.test.ts`, which covers pure input/output cases. The new tests cover:

- a year with no announcement: `announced: false`, statutory days only

issues.title: mcp: add a vietqr_decode tool matching the CLI `vietqr decode`
issues.body:
## Problem
RM-024 added `vn-skills vietqr decode <image>` to the CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/vietqr.ts`). `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` registers `vietqr_build`, `vietqr_parse` and `vietqr_banks` but has no tool that decodes a QR image. MCP clients therefore cannot do what the CLI and skill can, and the README tool list has no such entry.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Write the test first in `tests/mcp.test.ts`: it calls `vietqr_decode` and fails on the base because the tool does not exist.
- [ ] Add a `vietqr_decode` tool in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts` that takes an image file path, reuses the CLI decode logic (share it rather than duplicate it), and returns the parsed fields.
- [ ] An image with no QR returns the same structured error as the CLI.
- [ ] Add a round-trip test: a PNG built by `vietqr_build` with `out`, then `vietqr_decode`, gives the same fields.
- [ ] Add the tool to the README tool list and to `README.vi.md` if it lists tools.
- [ ] Mention the tool in `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` if the MCP tools are listed there.
- [ ] `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm exec vitest run` all pass.
issues.triage_reason: The tool and tests are simple, but `decodeQrPng` in packages/cli/src/commands/vietqr.ts must be shared with packages/mcp/src/server.ts, which lacks jsqr and pngjs. That requires a design choice on where the shared code lives plus a lockfile update.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- Moves jsqr and pngjs into packages/core as runtime dependencies. packages/core/package.json still describes the package as "Offline, dependency-free", and README.md calls core "pure TypeScript, no network, data bundled". The patch makes that description false and gives the published library an image-decoding dependency without any decision to do so. Keep the shared decode logic out of core: put it in a small shared location that already depends on jsqr and pngjs (e.g. export it from the CLI package, or a new internal helper). Alternatively, update the description and docs to match and have the maintainer agree to it.
- The `READ_ERROR` object for an unreadable file is duplicated. It is hand-written in packages/mcp/src/server.ts and again in packages/cli/src/commands/vietqr.ts. The issue asked to share the CLI decode logic, not duplicate it. Share one helper that takes a file path and returns the structured result.
- vietqr_build gains an `out` parameter that the issue did not ask for. It duplicates the CLI's write logic (PNG/SVG) and changes the tool's public output by adding a `file` field. It also writes to an arbitrary client-supplied path without any handling. It would be safer to share the CLI's write logic. The README and SKILL.md do not mention the new `out` parameter.
- The no-QR case is not tested. The test passes a non-PNG file, so it only covers READ_ERROR. The issue requires that an image with no QR returns the same structured error as the CLI, which is NO_QR. A valid PNG with no QR code needs a test.

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected:
- packages/mcp/README.md line 13 lists the MCP tools and was not updated to include `vietqr_decode`. The issue asks for the tool to be added to the README tool list, and this README is published with @vn-skills/mcp.
issues.summary: Added vietqr_decode MCP tool sharing the CLI's decodeQrPng helper (kept out of core, in the CLI package); documented in README.md, README.vi.md and packages/mcp/README.md; tests pass.
issues.pr_title: feat(mcp): add vietqr_decode tool
issues.pr_body:
**Dependencies added:** `@vn-skills/cli@workspace:* (packages/mcp/package.json)`

## What & why

Closes #75

MCP clients could not decode a VietQR image, although the CLI has `vn-skills vietqr decode <image>`. This adds a `vietqr_decode` tool to `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`.

The tool takes an image file path and returns the parsed fields. The decode logic moves into a shared helper, `decodeQrPng` in `packages/cli/src/decode.ts`. The CLI command and the MCP tool both call it. The helper stays out of `packages/core` so core stays offline and free of image dependencies. An image with no QR returns the same structured error as the CLI (`NO_QR`). A file that is not a PNG returns `READ_ERROR`.

Acceptance:

- [x] Test written first in `tests/mcp.test.ts`; it fails on the base because the tool does not exist.
- [x] `vietqr_decode` added in `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`, reusing the CLI decode logic through a shared helper.
- [x] An image with no QR returns the same structured error as the CLI.
- [x] Round-trip test: a PNG built by `vietqr_build` with `out`, then `vietqr_decode`, gives the same fields.
- [x] Tool added to `README.md`, `README.vi.md` and `packages/mcp/README.md`.
- [ ] `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` was not changed; the diff does not touch it.
- [x] `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm exec vitest run` pass.

## Testing

Added to `tests/mcp.test.ts`:

- `vietqr_decode reads back the fields of a PNG from vietqr_build`
- `vietqr_decode returns NO_QR for a PNG without a QR code`
- `vietqr_decode returns READ_ERROR for a file that is not a PNG`

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits (`feat|fix|docs|data|test|refactor|perf|build|ci|chore(scope): …`)
- [x] Tests added or updated (golden test for every bug fix)
- [x] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm format:check` pass locally
- [x] Core stays offline (no `fetch`/HTTP in `packages/core`)
- [ ] Data changes go through `scripts/build-data.ts` and `SOURCES.md` (source + license)
- [ ] SKILL.md / README updated if behaviour changed
issues.repro_notes: Fails on base because the vietqr_decode MCP tool is not registered (tool list mismatch; the decode calls return an MCP error). Tests: tool-list entry, build->PNG->decode round-trip (bin 970422, account 0123456789, amount 150000), NO_QR for a blank valid PNG, READ_ERROR for a non-PNG. Input param name 'path' chosen since the issue leaves it open.

issues.title: docs: add a 5-minute quickstart with copy-paste examples for each skill
issues.body:
## Problem
The README has a `<!-- TODO: GIF -->` placeholder and no short path from install to a first working result. Install steps are spread across the Skills, Install, MCP and Library sections. A newcomer cannot try the project in five minutes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] New `docs/quickstart.md` with three paths: CLI via `npx -y @vn-skills/cli`, MCP via `claude mcp add`, and the library via `npm i @vn-skills/core`.
- [ ] Each path has one copy-paste command and the exact expected output, taken by running the command (no invented values).
- [ ] A short section on `vn-skills install all --agent claude|cursor|codex`.
- [ ] The README links to the quickstart near the top.
- [ ] `README.vi.md` gets the same link and a matching Vietnamese quickstart, `docs/quickstart.vi.md`.
- [ ] The existing readme tests still pass.

Pausing this one: PR could not be opened: Command failed with exit code 1: gh api repos/beiryu/vn-skills/git/refs -f 'ref=refs/heads/docs/78-docs-add-a-5-minute-quickstart-with-copy' -f 'sha=73ce8c20ff273144cce2a20170e4ad747bbedde5'.
issues.triage_reason: Docs-only: add docs/quickstart.md and docs/quickstart.vi.md and link them from README.md and README.vi.md. Outputs must come from running the local build because the packages are unpublished, and tests/readme.test.ts must keep passing.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- docs/quickstart.md and docs/quickstart.vi.md, CLI path: the 'Output' block shows JSON (`{ "ok": true, "amount": ..., "words": ... }`) for `npx -y @vn-skills/cli money words 1200000`. In packages/cli/src/output.ts, `wantsJson` returns `!process.stdout.isTTY`, and money.ts prints only the plain words line when stdout is a TTY. A newcomer pasting the command into a terminal therefore gets `một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng`, not JSON. This breaks the issue's requirement of the exact expected output, and the docs never say the JSON appears only when piped. Fix by showing the real TTY output, or by adding `--json` to the command and showing that output.
- The CLI 'More' example (`address convert ...`) is described only as returning the old and new address. The real command prints something different in a terminal than when piped, and no output is shown for it, so the claim is vague and unverified against how the command behaves.
issues.summary: Added docs/quickstart.md and docs/quickstart.vi.md (CLI, MCP, library, install sections) and linked them from README.md and README.vi.md. Per review feedback, CLI examples now use --json with real captured output, and the docs explain TTY vs piped behaviour.

+# Quickstart (5 minutes)
+
+[Tiếng Việt](quickstart.vi.md)
+
+All three paths below need Node.js 22+ and run the same offline core. Each one turns `1200000` into Vietnamese words.
+
+## 1. CLI
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli money words 1200000 --json
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "amount": "1200000",
+  "words": "một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng"
+}
+```
+
+`--json` forces JSON output. Without it, a terminal prints only the plain line `một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng`; JSON is the default only when the output is piped.
+
+More: address conversion (old to new 34-province address):
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli address convert "P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM" --json
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "input": "P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM",
+  "mappingType": "merged",
+  "old": {
+    "province": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh",
+    "district": "Quận 1",
+    "ward": "Phường Bến Nghé",
+    "formatted": "Phường Bến Nghé, Quận 1, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+  },
+  "new": {
+    "province": {
+      "code": "79",
+      "fullName": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+    },
+    "ward": {
+      "code": "26740",
+      "fullName": "Phường Sài Gòn",
+      "postalCode": "71016"
+    },
+    "formatted": "Phường Sài Gòn, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+  },
+  "candidates": [
+    {
+      "code": "26740",
+      "fullName": "Phường Sài Gòn",
+      "province": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh",
+      "isDefault": true
+    }
+  ],
+  "confidence": 0.97,
+  "warnings": []
+}
+```
+
+## 2. MCP server
+
+```bash
+claude mcp add vn-skills -- npx -y @vn-skills/mcp
+```
+
+Restart Claude Code, then ask: _"đọc số 1200000 thành chữ"_. The agent calls the `vn_money_to_words` tool with
+`{ "amount": 1200000 }`, which returns:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "amount": "1200000",
+  "words": "một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng"
+}
+```
+
+For other MCP clients use `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`.
+
+## 3. Library
+
+```bash
+npm i @vn-skills/core
+```
+
+```js
+import { moneyToWords } from '@vn-skills/core';
+
+console.log(moneyToWords(1_200_000));
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```
+{
+  ok: true,
+  words: 'một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng',
+  amount: '1200000',
+  negative: false
+}
+```
+
+## Install the skills into your agent
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli install all --agent claude    # or cursor, codex
+```
+
+The binary is named `vn-skills`, so with a global install the same command is `vn-skills install all --agent claude` (replace `claude` with `cursor` or `codex`).
+
+This copies every skill into the agent's skills directory (`.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/` or `.codex/skills/`
+in the current project). Add `--global` for your home directory, `--dry-run` to only print the actions and `--force`
+to overwrite existing folders.

issues.title: repo: ship a Claude Code plugin marketplace so all skills + the MCP server install with one command
issues.body:
## Problem
To install vn-skills in Claude Code today you either `git clone` and `cp -r skills/<name>` one folder at a time, or run `npx -y @vn-skills/cli install …` and then add the MCP server separately with `claude mcp add`. Claude Code can install plugins straight from a git repo that contains `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces). This repo has no `.claude-plugin/` directory, `marketplace.json`, `plugin.json` or `.mcp.json`.

## Proposal
Make the repository root a single plugin listed in its own marketplace:

- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:
  ```json
  {
    "name": "vn-skills",
    "owner": { "name": "beiryu" },
    "plugins": [
      {
        "name": "vn-skills",
        "source": "./",
        "description": "Vietnam business logic for agents: VietQR, 34-province addresses, tax IDs, CCCD, phones, holidays, lunar calendar, e-invoices."
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with `name: "vn-skills"`, a `description`, `author`, `homepage`/`repository` = https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills, `license: "MIT"`. Do not add a `version` field (release-please does not manage this file).
- `.mcp.json` at the repo root: `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`.
- The existing `skills/` folder is the plugin's skills directory; do not move it.

Check the field names against the docs page above before finishing; if a field is not in the documented schema, leave it out.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json` exist, are valid JSON and end with a newline
- [ ] New test `tests/plugin.test.ts`: parses the three files, checks that the plugin name is `vn-skills`, that `source` resolves to the repo root, that every folder in `skills/` has a `SKILL.md`, and that `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp`
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md install sections gain a "Claude Code plugin" subsection placed first: `/plugin marketplace add beiryu/vn-skills` then `/plugin install vn-skills@vn-skills`
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: The project has 0 stars but ~650–830 npm downloads a month, so people who find it do try it. One install command that brings in all 11 skills plus the MCP server is the cheapest way to turn Claude Code visitors into users.

Build, typecheck, lint, tests and format all pass.

issues.title: mcp: add mcpName and server.json so @vn-skills/mcp can be published to the official MCP Registry
issues.body:
## Problem
The official MCP Registry has no entry for this server: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=vn-skills returns `{"servers":[],"count":0}`. Before an npm package can be published there, it needs:
1. `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"` in `packages/mcp/package.json`. Logging in with GitHub requires the `io.github.<user>/` prefix. The field is missing today.
2. A `server.json` that describes the package. The registry rejects descriptions longer than 100 characters, and the current npm description is about 130.

Reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/main/docs/modelcontextprotocol-io/quickstart.mdx

This issue covers the code change only. Publishing to the registry (`mcp-publisher login github` + `mcp-publisher publish`) is a maintainer step after the next npm release.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `packages/mcp/package.json` has `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"`
- [ ] `packages/mcp/server.json` follows the registry quickstart: `name` = `io.github.beiryu/vn-skills`, a `description` of 100 characters or fewer, `repository` pointing at https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills, `version` equal to the package version, and one `packages` entry for npm `@vn-skills/mcp` with stdio transport
- [ ] The release config bumps the `version` fields in `server.json` together with the package (add it as an extra file in the release-please config; this issue explicitly allows touching release config for that)
- [ ] A test asserts that `server.json` `name` equals `mcpName`, that its versions equal `packages/mcp/package.json` `version`, and that the description is 100 characters or fewer
- [ ] Short note in CONTRIBUTING.md (release section, or a new one) on running `mcp-publisher publish` after an npm release
issues.triage_reason: @vn-skills/mcp is the most downloaded package (827/month). Many MCP clients read the official registry, and right now the server cannot be listed there at all. #79 (registries/directories) is no longer open, but this code-side requirement is still missing.

The issue itself allows it, so a maintainer needs to approve that edit or do it manually. Nothing was changed. The remaining work is the mcpName field in packages/mcp/package.json, packages/mcp/server.json (version 0.4.0, description of 100 characters or fewer, npm @vn-skills/mcp with stdio transport) and a CONTRIBUTING.md note on running mcp-publisher publish.

issues.title: vn-number-format: formatNumber throws for maxFractionDigits outside 0–100 and garbles |n| ≥ 1e21
issues.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `formatNumber` passes `opts.maxFractionDigits` straight to `Math.abs(n).toFixed(digits)`:
- `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })` (or `-1`, or `1.5`) throws `RangeError: toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100`. This breaks the library contract ("Every function returns `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }` — no exceptions for bad input", README.md).
- For `|n| >= 1e21`, `toFixed` returns exponent notation (`"1e+21"`). The grouping regex then produces a malformed string instead of `1.000.000.000.000.000.000.000`. `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` inherit both problems.

## Fix
- Validate `maxFractionDigits`: an integer in 0–20 (or 0–100), otherwise `fail('INVALID_OPTION', …)` with a hint naming the allowed range.
- For finite numbers whose `toFixed` output contains `e`, either format the integer part via `BigInt(Math.trunc(n))` or return `fail('INVALID_NUMBER', …)` with a clear message. Document the chosen behaviour in the JSDoc and in `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })`, `-1` and `1.5` return `ok: false` and do not throw
- [ ] `formatNumber(1e21)` returns either a correctly grouped string or `ok: false`, never a string containing `e`
- [ ] Golden cases added to `tests/golden/` for vn-number-format (the file loaded by `tests/golden.ts`), plus `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cases for the throwing inputs
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
issues.triage_reason: Breaks the library's documented no-throw contract. Library callers can crash the process with an option value.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected (the test must be rewritten):
- Tests in tests/vn-number-format.test.ts for 1e21/-1e21/1e25 assert only inside `if (r.ok)`, so they pass vacuously if the function failed. Make them unconditional: expect(r.ok).toBe(true) and exact text checks (e.g. '-1.000.000.000.000.000.000.000' for -1e21).
- No test pins the exact output for 1e25, where BigInt(abs) yields the exact double value (10000000000000000905969664) rather than 1 followed by 25 zeros. Add an exact assertion so the behaviour documented as 'grouped exactly via BigInt' is verified.
issues.summary: formatNumber now validates maxFractionDigits (integer 0-20, else INVALID_OPTION) and groups |n|>=1e21 exactly via BigInt instead of toFixed exponent output; JSDoc and SKILL.md updated. Existing tests (unconditional exact assertions for 1e21/-1e21/1e25) pass.
issues.pr_title: fix(vn-number-format): validate maxFractionDigits and group |n| >= 1e21
issues.pr_body:
## What & why

Closes #91

`formatNumber` passed `maxFractionDigits` straight to `toFixed`. Values outside 0-100 or non-integers threw `RangeError`. For |n| >= 1e21, `toFixed` returns exponent notation, which produced a malformed grouped string. `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` inherited both problems.

issues.title: vn-number-format: explain why amounts like "1.5" are rejected
issues.body:
## Problem
`vn-skills numfmt parse "1.5"` returns `{ code: 'INVALID_AMOUNT', message: 'Cannot parse amount "1.5"', hint: 'Try "1tr2", "500k", "1.200.000"' }`. The rejection is intended: in `plainNumber` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`), `.` is a thousands separator only when every group has 3 digits, and `,` is the decimal mark. But the message does not say so, and users and agents typing the English decimal `1.5` do not know what to change. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `parse`) returns the same error.

## Fix
In `parseAmount`, when the numeric part contains `.` and fails the 3-digit grouping rule, return a specific hint: `"." groups thousands in Vietnamese (1.500 = 1500); use "," for decimals, e.g. "1,5"`. Keep the error code `INVALID_AMOUNT`. Other failures keep the current hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount('1.5')` and `parseAmount('1.50tr')` → `INVALID_AMOUNT` with a hint that mentions `,` as the decimal mark
- [ ] `parseAmount('abc')` keeps the existing hint
- [ ] `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md` common-mistakes section mentions this case
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts`
issues.triage_reason: This error was the confusing one a newcomer hit while trying the CLI. A specific hint lets agents fix the input themselves.
issues.summary: parseAmount returns a specific INVALID_AMOUNT hint (use ',' for decimals) when the numeric part has '.' failing the 3-digit grouping rule; other failures keep the old hint; SKILL.md common-mistakes section added.

issues.title: vn-number-format: parseAmount and formatDate throw on non-string input instead of returning an error
issues.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `parseAmount` calls `input.toLowerCase()` and `formatDate` calls `input.trim()` without coercing the input. Untyped callers (plain JS, JSON from other tools) get exceptions:
- `parseAmount(5)` → `TypeError: input.toLowerCase is not a function`
- `formatDate(null)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'trim')`

Other modules already guard with `String(input ?? '')` (`parsePhone`, `validateTaxId`, `parseCitizenId`), and the README promises no exceptions for bad input.

## Fix
Start both functions with `const raw = String(input ?? '')` (keep the `string` parameter type). Numbers then parse naturally (`parseAmount(5)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`), and `null`/`undefined` return `INVALID_AMOUNT`/`INVALID_DATE`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount(5 as any)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`; `parseAmount(null as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `formatDate(null as any)` and `formatDate(20250101 as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_DATE`, no throw
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cover these cases
issues.triage_reason: The numfmt functions are the only ones in the library that throw on bad input types. Aligning them with the other modules is trivial.

issues.title: vn-number-format: formatDate rejects valid years 0001–0099
issues.body:
## Problem
`formatDate` in `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts` builds the date with `new Date(Date.UTC(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d))`. `Date.UTC` maps years 0–99 to 1900–1999, so the `getUTCFullYear() !== m.y` check fails, and `formatDate('0050-01-01')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_DATE', message: '"0050-01-01" is not a real calendar date' } }`. The regexes accept 4-digit years and the output pads to 4 digits (`p(m.y, 4)`), so these years are meant to work. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `date`) and the CLI `numfmt date` have the same problem.

## Fix
Build the date with `const dt = new Date(0); dt.setUTCFullYear(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d);` (or equivalent) so years below 100 are not remapped. Keep the existing validity check.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatDate('0050-01-01')` → `01/01/0050`
- [ ] `formatDate('29/02/0004')` → `29/02/0004` (leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar); `formatDate('0003-02-29')` → `INVALID_DATE`
- [ ] Existing behaviour for 4-digit years ≥ 1000 unchanged
- [ ] Cases added to the vn-number-format golden fixture in `tests/golden/`
issues.triage_reason: Valid inputs are reported as impossible dates. A one-line fix with golden cases.
issues.summary: formatDate used Date.UTC which remaps years 0-99 to 1900-1999; now uses new Date(0).setUTCFullYear so years 0001-0099 validate correctly.

issues.body:
## Problem
`convertAddress(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'street')` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:58`). `searchWards(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')` because it passes the query straight to `tokenize` (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts:83-86`). `findProvince` already guards with `String(query ?? '')`, and `convertAddress('')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'EMPTY', ... } }`. The README promises "no exceptions for bad input". MCP clients that forward a missing or null field crash instead of getting `ok: false`. #95 fixed the same class of bug in vn-number-format.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Audit every exported function in `packages/core/src/address/` (`parseAddress`, `convertAddress`, `searchWards`, `findProvince`, and any other export taking a string)
- [ ] `null`, `undefined`, numbers and objects return an `ok: false` Result with a `hint` and do not throw. Use the existing `EMPTY` code for null/undefined/blank strings and the code/approach used for non-string input in `packages/core/src/numfmt` after #100 for other types
- [ ] Functions that do not return a Result handle these inputs without throwing; document the behaviour in JSDoc
- [ ] Tests in `tests/address.test.ts` cover null, undefined, a number and an object for each export
- [ ] Existing tests and golden fixtures still pass
issues.triage_reason: Address conversion is the flagship skill, and MCP callers do send null fields. It also brings the module in line with the error contract fixed for numfmt.
issues.skip_reason:
gave up after 3 attempts; last: Reviewer rejected:
- Round-2 point 1 is still open. `INVALID_INPUT` is a new error code. It appears only in the address code and tests. numfmt has no non-string handling to follow, because it only uses INVALID_NUMBER and INVALID_DATE. The patch neither reuses an existing convention nor documents the code in skills/vn-address/SKILL.md, the README, or the CLI/MCP docs. Document `INVALID_INPUT` (what triggers it and what the hint says) in those places, or switch to an existing code and explain the choice.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- The issue asks for an audit of every exported function that takes a string. `lookupProvince(query)` in packages/core/src/address/index.ts was not changed. For null, undefined, a number or an object it returns `PROVINCE_NOT_FOUND` with the message `No province matches "null"` and no `hint`. The issue requires the `EMPTY` code for null, undefined or blank input, and a hint for every bad-input case. Fix it by guarding with a shared check like `checkText`, or add a hint and use `EMPTY` or `INVALID_INPUT`, as the parsers now do.
- tests/address.test.ts does not cover `lookupProvince`, although the issue requires null, undefined, number and object cases for each export. Add those cases and assert `ok:false`, a hint, and `EMPTY` for null and undefined.
- The new non-string code `INVALID_INPUT` appears nowhere else in the repo, and no non-string handling exists in numfmt to follow. The issue says to reuse the numfmt approach. Make sure the code name and hint style are consistent with it, or state why a new code is needed.

Attempt 2:
Reviewer rejected:
- Round-1 feedback point 3 is still open. `INVALID_INPUT` is a new error code that appears nowhere else in packages/core. numfmt has no non-string handling to follow (it only uses INVALID_NUMBER and INVALID_DATE). Nothing explains why a new code is needed. Either reuse an existing code convention, or document `INVALID_INPUT` in the error-code docs and the CLI/MCP docs.
- convertAddress({foo:'bar'}) returns EMPTY with the message 'Address is empty', because `legacyTextFrom` produces ''. The issue asks for objects to be rejected as invalid input. The message is misleading, and the test only checks `ok:false` and the hint for this case. Validate that the structured object has a string `province` and return `INVALID_INPUT` with a clear message when it does not.
- The `convertAddress` guard is convoluted: it has two `checkText` calls, a `!` assertion and a double typeof check. Simplify it to one clear validation path.
- The tests never assert the `INVALID_INPUT` code for the parsers or `convertAddress`; they only assert the code for null and undefined. The non-string cases for these functions are therefore weakly covered.
issues.summary: All address exports now return ok:false with a hint (EMPTY for null/undefined/blank, INVALID_INPUT for other non-strings, including objects lacking a string province in convertAddress) or safe empty values (searchWards, findProvince) instead of throwing; lookupProvince fixed; simplified convertAddress guard; tests assert codes for every export.

issues.body:
## Problem
`parseCitizenId` (`packages/core/src/id/index.ts:55-57`) computes `century = 1900 + Math.floor(digit / 2) * 100` for any digit 0–9. `parseCitizenId('001900123456')` returns `ok: true` with `birthYear: 2300` and no warning. The century coding comes from Circular 59/2021/TT-BCA, which the file already cites, so the decoding itself stays. But a birth year after the current year cannot belong to an issued card, and agents should be told.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Add an optional second argument `opts?: { today?: Date }` (default `new Date()`) so tests are deterministic

- [ ] `skills/vn-id/SKILL.md` mentions the warning

issues.title: vietqr: do not split surrogate pairs when truncating a raw note
issues.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:103-108`, a note with `rawNote: true` keeps its characters and is cut with `note.slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH)` (25). `slice` counts UTF-16 code units. An emoji or other astral character at position 24–25 is split, leaving a lone surrogate in the payload. That makes invalid UTF-8 when encoded or rendered to a QR image.

Out of scope: whether EMVCo/NAPAS lengths count bytes or characters (`tlvEncode` in `packages/core/src/shared/tlv.ts:15-17` uses `value.length`). The repo does not cite the spec for this; it is tracked separately and must not change here.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Truncation works on code points (e.g. `Array.from(note).slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH).join('')`), so no lone surrogate is ever produced
- [ ] Behaviour for BMP-only notes, including Vietnamese with diacritics, is unchanged (existing tests pass)
- [ ] Test in `tests/vietqr.test.ts`: 24 ASCII characters plus an emoji, with `rawNote: true`, yields a note with no lone surrogate (`/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/` does not match) and `parseVietQR` round-trips it
issues.triage_reason: A corrupt payload in a payment QR is a silent failure. The surrogate fix needs no spec decision.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- In packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts the guard `note.length > MAX_NOTE_LENGTH` counts UTF-16 code units, but truncation now counts code points. For 24 ASCII characters plus an emoji (the issue's own case) nothing is cut, yet the warning 'Note truncated to 25 characters.' is still emitted, which is untrue. Compute `Array.from(note)` once, compare its length to MAX_NOTE_LENGTH, and warn only when characters are actually dropped.

`buildVietQR` cut a `rawNote` with `note.slice(0, 25)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. An emoji at position 24-25 was split, leaving a lone surrogate in the payload and invalid UTF-8 when encoded.

`tlvEncode` still uses `value.length`. Whether the spec counts bytes or characters is out of scope and is unchanged.

issues.title: vietqr: say when a parsed payload was lower-cased in transit instead of reporting a bare CRC mismatch
issues.body:
## Problem

`parseVietQR` recomputes the CRC over the payload exactly as received (`packages/core/src/vietqr/parse.ts:44-46`). When a valid payload has been lower-cased by a chat app or a form, the CRC no longer matches and the warning makes the payload look corrupted:

```
parseVietQR(buildVietQR({...}).payload.toLowerCase())
=> ok: true, crcValid: false, warnings: [
  "CRC mismatch: payload has 8300, expected E6CC.",
  "Tag 38 GUID is \"a000000727\", not NAPAS A000000727."
]
```

The CRC hex digits are already compared case-insensitively (line 46). The mismatch happens because the CRC is computed over the lower-cased payload. A scanner would compute the CRC over the payload as given too, so `crcValid: false` is the correct result. The problem is that neither warning tells the user the real cause, which is that the case was changed, not the data.

## Proposal

- When `crcValid` is false, also compute `crc16CcittFalse` over the upper-cased prefix (`payload.slice(0, crcIndex + 4).toUpperCase()`). If that matches `crc.toUpperCase()`, replace the plain CRC mismatch warning with one that says the payload appears to have been lower-cased in transit and the CRC matches the upper-cased payload. It should also tell the user to use the original payload.
- If the tag 38 GUID differs from `A000000727` only by case, warn that the GUID is lower-cased instead of saying it is not NAPAS.
- Do not change `crcValid` semantics: it stays `false` for a payload whose CRC does not match as given.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A lower-cased payload built from an upper-case-only input (for example, no note or an upper-case note) gets the new lower-case warning and no "not NAPAS" GUID warning; `crcValid` is still `false`
- [ ] A payload with a genuinely wrong CRC still gets the existing `CRC mismatch: ...` warning
- [ ] A lower-cased payload whose original had a mixed-case note (the upper-case retry does not match) keeps the plain mismatch warning and gets no false hint
- [ ] Valid payloads parse exactly as before (existing tests unchanged)
- [ ] Golden case(s) added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` in the existing case format
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: People paste payloads through tools that change case. Today the warning blames data corruption, so callers can't tell a mangled-but-recoverable code from a broken one.
issues.summary: parseVietQR now detects lower-cased payloads (CRC matches upper-cased prefix) and emits a lower-case/original-payload warning instead of CRC mismatch; lower-cased tag 38 GUID gets a specific warning instead of 'not NAPAS'. crcValid unchanged. Added golden case.

issues.title: vn-lunar: reject out-of-range day and month in parseDateInput
issues.body:
## Problem

`parseDateInput` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:87-96`) only checks the shape of the string. `parseDateInput('0/1/2024')` returns `{ ok: true, day: 0, month: 1, year: 2024 }`, and inputs such as `32/1/2024`, `1/13/2024` and `2024-00-10` also pass. Callers re-validate later and return a generic `INVALID_DATE`, so the visible effect is a less precise error. Any caller that skips the second check would accept day 0. Non-padded forms (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`) are intentional and should stay accepted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `parseDateInput` returns `INVALID_DATE` when the month is outside 1-12 or the day is outside 1 to the number of days in that month (Gregorian, leap years included: `29/2/2024` ok, `29/2/2023` rejected)
- [ ] The error message names the bad part (e.g. `Day 0 is out of range for 01/2024`) and keeps the existing hint
- [ ] Non-padded inputs (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`, `3/2/2024`) still parse
- [ ] Tests added to `tests/lunar.test.ts` for day 0, day 32, month 0, month 13, 31/4, 29/2 in leap and non-leap years, and the non-padded forms
- [ ] Existing CLI tests (`tests/cli.test.ts`) still pass; update expected messages only where the new message is more precise
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
issues.triage_reason: This is a small hardening fix. The helper is shared, so validating once here gives precise errors everywhere and removes the risk of a caller accepting day 0.
issues.feedback:
Attempt 1:
Reviewer rejected:
- Gregorian day-of-month validation inside parseDateInput breaks the `lunar to-solar` CLI command, which parses lunar dates with the same function. Valid lunar dates such as day 30 of month 2, or 29/2 in a Gregorian non-leap year, are now rejected with INVALID_DATE. Keep to-solar working, e.g. validate Gregorian days only for the solar callers or add a separate strict parser, and add a test for a lunar 30/2 case in to-solar.
- Bug fix has no golden case in tests/golden/vn-lunar.json (parseDateInput cases already live there); the pure input->output rejections (0/1/2024, 29/2/2023) should be added there per project convention.

issues.pr_body:
Closes #132

## What & why

`parseDateInput` only checked the shape of the string, so inputs such as `0/1/2024`, `32/1/2024`, `1/13/2024` and `2024-00-10` returned `ok: true`. Callers re-validated later and returned a generic `INVALID_DATE`.

issues.title: docs: add copy-paste MCP setup for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and Codex
issues.body:
## Problem

`@vn-skills/mcp` is the most downloaded package (827/month), but the README's MCP section (`README.md`, "MCP server") shows only `claude mcp add` and one generic `mcpServers` JSON block. Not every client uses that shape. VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json` uses a top-level `servers` key, and Codex reads TOML from `~/.codex/config.toml`. A user who pastes the generic JSON into one of those clients gets a server that never starts, and the README doesn't say where each file goes. `docs/quickstart.md` has the same gap.

This is the install-guide half of RM-003. The demo GIF half is tracked in #92.

## Proposal

Add a short "MCP client setup" subsection to `README.md` (and the same in `README.vi.md`) with one block per client:

- **Claude Code:** keep `claude mcp add vn-skills -- npx -y @vn-skills/mcp`
- **Claude Desktop:** `claude_desktop_config.json`, `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Cursor:** `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global), same `mcpServers` shape
- **VS Code:** `.vscode/mcp.json`, `{ "servers": { "vn-skills": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Codex:** `~/.codex/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  [mcp_servers.vn-skills]
  command = "npx"
  args = ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"]
  ```

Link each client to its official MCP documentation page so readers can check the file location. Keep the generic block for other clients. Mention that Node.js 22+ is required.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `README.md` has a block for each of the five clients above, each with a link to that client's MCP docs
- [ ] `README.vi.md` has the same content in Vietnamese
- [ ] `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` link to the new section instead of duplicating it
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes (extend it if it checks the MCP section)
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` passes
issues.triage_reason: MCP is the channel with the most downloads, and getting set up in a client is the step where people drop off. Snippets that work as pasted for each client turn downloads into working installs.

+# Quickstart (5 minutes)
+
+[Tiếng Việt](quickstart.vi.md)
+
+All three paths below need Node.js 22+ and run the same offline core. Each one turns `1200000` into Vietnamese words.
+
+## 1. CLI
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli money words 1200000 --json
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "amount": "1200000",
+  "words": "một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng"
+}
+```
+
+`--json` forces JSON output. Without it, a terminal prints only the plain line `một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng`; JSON is the default only when the output is piped.
+
+More: address conversion (old to new 34-province address):
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli address convert "P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM" --json
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "input": "P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM",
+  "mappingType": "merged",
+  "old": {
+    "province": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh",
+    "district": "Quận 1",
+    "ward": "Phường Bến Nghé",
+    "formatted": "Phường Bến Nghé, Quận 1, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+  },
+  "new": {
+    "province": {
+      "code": "79",
+      "fullName": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+    },
+    "ward": {
+      "code": "26740",
+      "fullName": "Phường Sài Gòn",
+      "postalCode": "71016"
+    },
+    "formatted": "Phường Sài Gòn, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh"
+  },
+  "candidates": [
+    {
+      "code": "26740",
+      "fullName": "Phường Sài Gòn",
+      "province": "Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh",
+      "isDefault": true
+    }
+  ],
+  "confidence": 0.97,
+  "warnings": []
+}
+```
+
+## 2. MCP server
+
+```bash
+claude mcp add vn-skills -- npx -y @vn-skills/mcp
+```
+
+Restart Claude Code, then ask: _"đọc số 1200000 thành chữ"_. The agent calls the `vn_money_to_words` tool with
+`{ "amount": 1200000 }`, which returns:
+
+```json
+{
+  "ok": true,
+  "amount": "1200000",
+  "words": "một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng"
+}
+```
+
+For other MCP clients use `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`.
+
+## 3. Library
+
+```bash
+npm i @vn-skills/core
+```
+
+```js
+import { moneyToWords } from '@vn-skills/core';
+
+console.log(moneyToWords(1_200_000));
+```
+
+Output:
+
+```
+{
+  ok: true,
+  words: 'một triệu hai trăm nghìn đồng',
+  amount: '1200000',
+  negative: false
+}
+```
+
+## Install the skills into your agent
+
+```bash
+npx -y @vn-skills/cli install all --agent claude    # or cursor, codex
+```
+
+The binary is named `vn-skills`, so with a global install the same command is `vn-skills install all --agent claude` (replace `claude` with `cursor` or `codex`).
+
+This copies every skill into the agent's skills directory (`.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/` or `.codex/skills/`
+in the current project). Add `--global` for your home directory, `--dry-run` to only print the actions and `--force`
+to overwrite existing folders.

Closes #91

`formatNumber` passed `maxFractionDigits` straight to `toFixed`. Values outside 0-100 or non-integers threw `RangeError`. For |n| >= 1e21, `toFixed` returns exponent notation, which produced a malformed grouped string. `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` inherited both problems.

## What & why

`formatDate` built the date with `Date.UTC`, which maps years 0-99 to 1900-1999. The year check then failed, so valid dates like `0050-01-01` returned `INVALID_DATE`. The date is now built with `new Date(0)` and `setUTCFullYear(y, m, d)`, which does not remap years. The existing validity check is unchanged. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `date`) and the CLI `numfmt date` call `formatDate`, so they get the fix too.

## What & why

proposals.title: repo: ship a Claude Code plugin marketplace so all skills + the MCP server install with one command
proposals.body:
## Problem
To install vn-skills in Claude Code today you either `git clone` and `cp -r skills/<name>` one folder at a time, or run `npx -y @vn-skills/cli install …` and then add the MCP server separately with `claude mcp add`. Claude Code can install plugins straight from a git repo that contains `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces). This repo has no `.claude-plugin/` directory, `marketplace.json`, `plugin.json` or `.mcp.json`.

## Proposal
Make the repository root a single plugin listed in its own marketplace:

- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:
  ```json
  {
    "name": "vn-skills",
    "owner": { "name": "beiryu" },
    "plugins": [
      {
        "name": "vn-skills",
        "source": "./",
        "description": "Vietnam business logic for agents: VietQR, 34-province addresses, tax IDs, CCCD, phones, holidays, lunar calendar, e-invoices."
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with `name: "vn-skills"`, a `description`, `author`, `homepage`/`repository` = https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills, `license: "MIT"`. Do not add a `version` field (release-please does not manage this file).
- `.mcp.json` at the repo root: `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`.
- The existing `skills/` folder is the plugin's skills directory; do not move it.

Check the field names against the docs page above before finishing; if a field is not in the documented schema, leave it out.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json` exist, are valid JSON and end with a newline
- [ ] New test `tests/plugin.test.ts`: parses the three files, checks that the plugin name is `vn-skills`, that `source` resolves to the repo root, that every folder in `skills/` has a `SKILL.md`, and that `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y @vn-skills/mcp`
- [ ] README.md and README.vi.md install sections gain a "Claude Code plugin" subsection placed first: `/plugin marketplace add beiryu/vn-skills` then `/plugin install vn-skills@vn-skills`
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: The project has 0 stars but ~650–830 npm downloads a month, so people who find it do try it. One install command that brings in all 11 skills plus the MCP server is the cheapest way to turn Claude Code visitors into users.

proposals.title: mcp: add mcpName and server.json so @vn-skills/mcp can be published to the official MCP Registry
proposals.body:
## Problem
The official MCP Registry has no entry for this server: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=vn-skills returns `{"servers":[],"count":0}`. Before an npm package can be published there, it needs:
1. `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"` in `packages/mcp/package.json`. Logging in with GitHub requires the `io.github.<user>/` prefix. The field is missing today.
2. A `server.json` that describes the package. The registry rejects descriptions longer than 100 characters, and the current npm description is about 130.

Reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/main/docs/modelcontextprotocol-io/quickstart.mdx

This issue covers the code change only. Publishing to the registry (`mcp-publisher login github` + `mcp-publisher publish`) is a maintainer step after the next npm release.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `packages/mcp/package.json` has `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"`
- [ ] `packages/mcp/server.json` follows the registry quickstart: `name` = `io.github.beiryu/vn-skills`, a `description` of 100 characters or fewer, `repository` pointing at https://github.com/beiryu/vn-skills, `version` equal to the package version, and one `packages` entry for npm `@vn-skills/mcp` with stdio transport
- [ ] The release config bumps the `version` fields in `server.json` together with the package (add it as an extra file in the release-please config; this issue explicitly allows touching release config for that)
- [ ] A test asserts that `server.json` `name` equals `mcpName`, that its versions equal `packages/mcp/package.json` `version`, and that the description is 100 characters or fewer
- [ ] Short note in CONTRIBUTING.md (release section, or a new one) on running `mcp-publisher publish` after an npm release
proposals.rationale: @vn-skills/mcp is the most downloaded package (827/month). Many MCP clients read the official registry, and right now the server cannot be listed there at all. #79 (registries/directories) is no longer open, but this code-side requirement is still missing.

proposals.title: vn-number-format: formatNumber throws for maxFractionDigits outside 0–100 and garbles |n| ≥ 1e21
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `formatNumber` passes `opts.maxFractionDigits` straight to `Math.abs(n).toFixed(digits)`:
- `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })` (or `-1`, or `1.5`) throws `RangeError: toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100`. This breaks the library contract ("Every function returns `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }` — no exceptions for bad input", README.md).
- For `|n| >= 1e21`, `toFixed` returns exponent notation (`"1e+21"`). The grouping regex then produces a malformed string instead of `1.000.000.000.000.000.000.000`. `formatVnd` and `formatCompactVnd` inherit both problems.

## Fix
- Validate `maxFractionDigits`: an integer in 0–20 (or 0–100), otherwise `fail('INVALID_OPTION', …)` with a hint naming the allowed range.
- For finite numbers whose `toFixed` output contains `e`, either format the integer part via `BigInt(Math.trunc(n))` or return `fail('INVALID_NUMBER', …)` with a clear message. Document the chosen behaviour in the JSDoc and in `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatNumber(1, { maxFractionDigits: 101 })`, `-1` and `1.5` return `ok: false` and do not throw
- [ ] `formatNumber(1e21)` returns either a correctly grouped string or `ok: false`, never a string containing `e`
- [ ] Golden cases added to `tests/golden/` for vn-number-format (the file loaded by `tests/golden.ts`), plus `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cases for the throwing inputs
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
proposals.rationale: Breaks the library's documented no-throw contract. Library callers can crash the process with an option value.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts formatNumber (toFixed call)","README.md#library (no exceptions for bad input)","$ formatNumber(1,{maxFractionDigits:101}) -> THROW toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100"]

proposals.title: vn-number-format: formatDate rejects valid years 0001–0099
proposals.body:
## Problem
`formatDate` in `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts` builds the date with `new Date(Date.UTC(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d))`. `Date.UTC` maps years 0–99 to 1900–1999, so the `getUTCFullYear() !== m.y` check fails, and `formatDate('0050-01-01')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_DATE', message: '"0050-01-01" is not a real calendar date' } }`. The regexes accept 4-digit years and the output pads to 4 digits (`p(m.y, 4)`), so these years are meant to work. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `date`) and the CLI `numfmt date` have the same problem.

## Fix
Build the date with `const dt = new Date(0); dt.setUTCFullYear(m.y, m.mo - 1, m.d);` (or equivalent) so years below 100 are not remapped. Keep the existing validity check.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `formatDate('0050-01-01')` → `01/01/0050`
- [ ] `formatDate('29/02/0004')` → `29/02/0004` (leap year in the proleptic Gregorian calendar); `formatDate('0003-02-29')` → `INVALID_DATE`
- [ ] Existing behaviour for 4-digit years ≥ 1000 unchanged
- [ ] Cases added to the vn-number-format golden fixture in `tests/golden/`
proposals.rationale: Valid inputs are reported as impossible dates. A one-line fix with golden cases.

proposals.title: vn-number-format: parseAmount and formatDate throw on non-string input instead of returning an error
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`, `parseAmount` calls `input.toLowerCase()` and `formatDate` calls `input.trim()` without coercing the input. Untyped callers (plain JS, JSON from other tools) get exceptions:
- `parseAmount(5)` → `TypeError: input.toLowerCase is not a function`
- `formatDate(null)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'trim')`

Other modules already guard with `String(input ?? '')` (`parsePhone`, `validateTaxId`, `parseCitizenId`), and the README promises no exceptions for bad input.

## Fix
Start both functions with `const raw = String(input ?? '')` (keep the `string` parameter type). Numbers then parse naturally (`parseAmount(5)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`), and `null`/`undefined` return `INVALID_AMOUNT`/`INVALID_DATE`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount(5 as any)` → `{ ok: true, value: 5 }`; `parseAmount(null as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_AMOUNT`
- [ ] `formatDate(null as any)` and `formatDate(20250101 as any)` → `ok: false`, code `INVALID_DATE`, no throw
- [ ] Tests in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts` cover these cases
proposals.rationale: The numfmt functions are the only ones in the library that throw on bad input types. Aligning them with the other modules is trivial.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts parseAmount/formatDate","packages/core/src/phone, taxid, id use String(input ?? '')","$ parseAmount(5) -> THROW input.toLowerCase is not a function"]

proposals.title: vn-number-format: explain why amounts like "1.5" are rejected
proposals.body:
## Problem
`vn-skills numfmt parse "1.5"` returns `{ code: 'INVALID_AMOUNT', message: 'Cannot parse amount "1.5"', hint: 'Try "1tr2", "500k", "1.200.000"' }`. The rejection is intended: in `plainNumber` (`packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts`), `.` is a thousands separator only when every group has 3 digits, and `,` is the decimal mark. But the message does not say so, and users and agents typing the English decimal `1.5` do not know what to change. The MCP tool `vn_number_format` (mode `parse`) returns the same error.

## Fix
In `parseAmount`, when the numeric part contains `.` and fails the 3-digit grouping rule, return a specific hint: `"." groups thousands in Vietnamese (1.500 = 1500); use "," for decimals, e.g. "1,5"`. Keep the error code `INVALID_AMOUNT`. Other failures keep the current hint.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `parseAmount('1.5')` and `parseAmount('1.50tr')` → `INVALID_AMOUNT` with a hint that mentions `,` as the decimal mark
- [ ] `parseAmount('abc')` keeps the existing hint
- [ ] `skills/vn-number-format/SKILL.md` common-mistakes section mentions this case
- [ ] Tests added in `tests/vn-number-format.test.ts`
proposals.rationale: This error was the confusing one a newcomer hit while trying the CLI. A specific hint lets agents fix the input themselves.
proposals.evidence: ["packages/core/src/numfmt/index.ts plainNumber/parseAmount","$ vn-skills numfmt parse \"1.5\" -> INVALID_AMOUNT with generic hint"]

proposals.title: docs: make the README einvoice example runnable and fix the in-repo CLI invocation

The README.md and README.vi.md skills tables show `vn-skills einvoice totals invoice.json`, but no step creates `invoice.json`, so a newcomer gets `READ_ERROR: Cannot read invoice JSON from invoice.json: ENOENT`. `vn-skills einvoice example` (`packages/cli/src/commands/einvoice.ts`) prints a starter invoice, but the README never mentions it.
2. README.md says "Inside this repository (before the packages are published) use `pnpm vn-skills …`". The packages are published now. The pnpm wrapper (`package.json` script `"vn-skills": "node packages/cli/dist/index.js"`) echoes the command line, and on every `ok:false` result it appends `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.` after the JSON, even with `pnpm -s`. That breaks clean JSON for agents. Running `node packages/cli/dist/index.js …` directly is clean.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Same change in CONTRIBUTING.md if it still recommends `pnpm vn-skills` for scripted use (keeping it for `--help` is fine)
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes (update it if it checks these lines)

proposals.title: repo: fix the release token so 0.5.0 is tagged and published to npm
proposals.body:
## Problem
The 0.5.0 release commit (606314fe, #98) is on main, but npm still serves 0.4.0 as `latest` for `@vn-skills/core`, `@vn-skills/cli` and `@vn-skills/mcp`, and the newest GitHub Release is v0.4.0. In Release workflow run 39784434188 (2026-10-22 13:09 UTC), the release-please step failed with `release-please failed: Resource not accessible by integration` when it tried to create the release. The publish job was then skipped.

So #97, #99, #100, #101, the `vietqr_decode` MCP tool (#84) and `mcpName` (#103) have not reached users. The MCP Registry listing is blocked until this ships.

The workflow uses `AGENT_GITHUB_TOKEN` when it is set, otherwise `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The token probably lacks `contents: write` for releases.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Check which token the release job uses and give it permission to create tags and releases (`contents: write`), or switch the release step to a token that has it
- [ ] Re-run the Release workflow, or use its `workflow_dispatch` recovery path, so the `v0.5.0` tag and GitHub Release are created
- [ ] Confirm that `https://registry.npmjs.org/@vn-skills/mcp/latest` shows `0.5.0` and contains `"mcpName": "io.github.beiryu/vn-skills"`
- [ ] Confirm that `@vn-skills/core` and `@vn-skills/cli` are also at 0.5.0
- [ ] Optional: note the `ubuntu-latest` → Ubuntu 26 warning from the same run and decide whether to pin the runner image

proposals.title: vn-address: return an error instead of throwing on null or non-string input
proposals.body:
## Problem
`convertAddress(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'street')` (`packages/core/src/address/convert.ts:58`). `searchWards(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')` because it passes the query straight to `tokenize` (`packages/core/src/address/index.ts:83-86`). `findProvince` already guards with `String(query ?? '')`, and `convertAddress('')` returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: 'EMPTY', ... } }`. The README promises "no exceptions for bad input". MCP clients that forward a missing or null field crash instead of getting `ok: false`. #95 fixed the same class of bug in vn-number-format.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Audit every exported function in `packages/core/src/address/` (`parseAddress`, `convertAddress`, `searchWards`, `findProvince`, and any other export taking a string)
- [ ] `null`, `undefined`, numbers and objects return an `ok: false` Result with a `hint` and do not throw. Use the existing `EMPTY` code for null/undefined/blank strings and the code/approach used for non-string input in `packages/core/src/numfmt` after #100 for other types
- [ ] Functions that do not return a Result handle these inputs without throwing; document the behaviour in JSDoc
- [ ] Tests in `tests/address.test.ts` cover null, undefined, a number and an object for each export
- [ ] Existing tests and golden fixtures still pass
proposals.rationale: Address conversion is the flagship skill, and MCP callers do send null fields. It also brings the module in line with the error contract fixed for numfmt.

proposals.title: vn-name: handle null and non-string input without throwing
proposals.body:
## Problem
`splitName`, `slugifyName`, `initials` and `sortNames` (`packages/core/src/name/index.ts`) call `.normalize` on their argument, directly or via `removeDiacritics`/`normalizeText` (`packages/core/src/shared/diacritics.ts:6`). Null or non-string input throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'normalize')`. Phone, taxid, CCCD, money and parseVietQR return `ok: false` for the same input.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `splitName(null | undefined | '   ')` returns the existing `EMPTY_NAME` failure. Other non-strings (numbers, objects) return an `ok: false` Result with a hint and do not throw
- [ ] `slugifyName` and `initials` (which return plain strings) return `''` for null/undefined/non-string input; documented in JSDoc
- [ ] `sortNames` does not throw when the array contains non-string entries. It drops them from the result; documented in JSDoc
- [ ] Do not change the return types (no breaking API change)
- [ ] Tests in `tests/name.test.ts` for each function with null, undefined, a number and an object
- [ ] Existing tests and golden fixtures still pass
proposals.rationale: This is the last core module that crashes on missing MCP/JSON fields, which goes against the README's 'no exceptions for bad input' promise.

proposals.title: vn-id: warn when a decoded CCCD birth year is in the future
proposals.body:
## Problem
`parseCitizenId` (`packages/core/src/id/index.ts:55-57`) computes `century = 1900 + Math.floor(digit / 2) * 100` for any digit 0–9. `parseCitizenId('001900123456')` returns `ok: true` with `birthYear: 2300` and no warning. The century coding comes from Circular 59/2021/TT-BCA, which the file already cites, so the decoding itself stays. But a birth year after the current year cannot belong to an issued card, and agents should be told.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Add an optional second argument `opts?: { today?: Date }` (default `new Date()`) so tests are deterministic
- [ ] When `birthYear` is after `today`'s year, the result keeps `ok: true` and adds a warning naming the decoded year, e.g. `Decoded birth year 2300 is in the future; the ID is probably mistyped.`
- [ ] No warning for birth years up to and including the current year
- [ ] Tests in `tests/id.test.ts` with a fixed `today`: digit 9 (future), digit 2/3 with a past year (no warning), and a birth year equal to the current year (no warning)
- [ ] CLI `id parse` and MCP `vn_id_parse` output includes the new warning (no new flags needed)
- [ ] `skills/vn-id/SKILL.md` mentions the warning
proposals.rationale: A typo in the century digit decodes silently to an impossible person. That is the kind of plausible-looking wrong answer the project exists to prevent.

proposals.title: vn-holidays: give OUT_OF_RANGE a correct hint and name the date in addWorkingDays
proposals.body:
## Problem
`checkYear` in `packages/core/src/holidays/index.ts:146-151` returns the same hint, `The data set starts with the 2023 notices.`, for years before `FIRST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` and after `LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR`. A year above 2199 gets a hint about the start of the data. Also, `addWorkingDays(30, 12, 2199, 5)` fails with only `Supported years: 2023-2199` and does not say that the walk crossed the upper bound.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Years below `FIRST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` keep the existing hint
- [ ] Years above `LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR` get a hint that states the upper limit (built from the constant, e.g. `Dates after 31/12/${LAST_HOLIDAY_YEAR} are not supported.`) without claiming a reason the repo does not document
- [ ] When `addWorkingDays` leaves the supported range during the walk, the message names the start date and says the result would fall outside the range
- [ ] Tests in `tests/holidays.test.ts` for a year below, a year above, and `addWorkingDays(30, 12, 2199, 5)`
- [ ] Golden case in `tests/golden/` for the year-above input → error code
proposals.rationale: The hint is wrong, which misleads agents that relay hints to users. A small, contained fix.

proposals.title: vn-phone: add hints to every error and a distinct EMPTY error
proposals.body:
## Problem
The README says every failure is `{ code, message, hint }`, but `parsePhone` (`packages/core/src/phone/index.ts`) calls `fail()` with no hint. Example: `node packages/cli/dist/index.js phone ''` prints `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_FORMAT","message":"Phone number may only contain digits, spaces, . - ( ) and a leading +"}}`. An empty input is reported as an invalid character, while address and name use an explicit EMPTY code.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Empty/whitespace/null input returns `code: 'EMPTY'` with message `Phone number is empty` and a hint
- [ ] Every other `fail(...)` in `packages/core/src/phone/` has a hint telling the user what to pass (e.g. `Use 10 digits starting with 0, or +84 followed by 9 digits.`), with no new numbering facts beyond those already in `prefixes.js`
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/phone.test.ts` that runs each error path and asserts `error.hint` is a non-empty string
- [ ] Golden case in `tests/golden/` for `''` → `EMPTY`; update existing golden cases if their codes change
- [ ] Note the new `EMPTY` code in `skills/vn-phone/SKILL.md` if it lists error codes
proposals.rationale: Agents use the hint to recover. A missing hint breaks the documented error contract on a common input.

proposals.title: cli: accept unquoted multi-word text for free-text arguments
proposals.body:
## Problem
Several commands take one free-text argument. Without quotes, the user gets a bare commander error:

```
$ node packages/cli/dist/index.js name split Tôn Thất Tùng
error: too many arguments for 'split'. Expected 1 argument but got 3: Tôn, Thất, Tùng.
```

Agents and newcomers often drop the quotes. Joining the words is unambiguous for these commands.

## Acceptance
- [ ] These commands declare a variadic argument and join the words with a single space: `name split|slug|initials` (`packages/cli/src/commands/name.ts`), `address parse|convert|wards|province` (`address.ts`), `numfmt parse` (`numfmt.ts`)
- [ ] `name sort <names...>` is unchanged (each argument is a name)
- [ ] Help text still shows one logical argument (e.g. `<fullName...>`) and says quotes are optional
- [ ] Tests in `tests/cli.test.ts`: `name split Tôn Thất Tùng` gives the same JSON as `name split "Tôn Thất Tùng"`, and `address convert P. Bến Nghé, Q.1, TP.HCM` gives the same JSON as the quoted form
- [ ] README/SKILL.md examples stay quoted (no doc change required)
proposals.rationale: The first command a newcomer copies should not fail on quoting. Agents generate unquoted arguments too.

proposals.title: vietqr: do not split surrogate pairs when truncating a raw note
proposals.body:
## Problem
In `packages/core/src/vietqr/build.ts:103-108`, a note with `rawNote: true` keeps its characters and is cut with `note.slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH)` (25). `slice` counts UTF-16 code units. An emoji or other astral character at position 24–25 is split, leaving a lone surrogate in the payload. That makes invalid UTF-8 when encoded or rendered to a QR image.

Out of scope: whether EMVCo/NAPAS lengths count bytes or characters (`tlvEncode` in `packages/core/src/shared/tlv.ts:15-17` uses `value.length`). The repo does not cite the spec for this; it is tracked separately and must not change here.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Truncation works on code points (e.g. `Array.from(note).slice(0, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH).join('')`), so no lone surrogate is ever produced
- [ ] Behaviour for BMP-only notes, including Vietnamese with diacritics, is unchanged (existing tests pass)
- [ ] Test in `tests/vietqr.test.ts`: 24 ASCII characters plus an emoji, with `rawNote: true`, yields a note with no lone surrogate (`/[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/` does not match) and `parseVietQR` round-trips it
proposals.rationale: A corrupt payload in a payment QR is a silent failure. The surrogate fix needs no spec decision.

proposals.title: vietqr: decide whether TLV lengths count bytes or characters for non-ASCII raw notes
proposals.body:
## Problem
`tlvEncode` (`packages/core/src/shared/tlv.ts:15-17`) writes `value.length`, which counts UTF-16 code units. With `rawNote: true` a note can contain Vietnamese diacritics. Example: `buildVietQR({bank:'VCB',account:'123',note:'é'.repeat(30),rawNote:true})` gives a 25-character note whose UTF-8 encoding is 50 bytes. If NAPAS/EMVCo or banking apps read the length field as bytes, these payloads are misparsed. The repository does not cite which rule applies, so this needs a person with the spec.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Find the governing rule (EMVCo QRCPS-MPM and/or the NAPAS VietQR spec) and cite the section
- [ ] Optional: test a `rawNote` payload with diacritics in two or three banking apps
- [ ] Write the decision into the issue: keep character counting, switch to UTF-8 byte counting (and adjust `MAX_NOTE_LENGTH` / truncation), or forbid non-ASCII raw notes
- [ ] Then hand it to implementation with the cited source
proposals.rationale: [needs you] This could produce payment QRs that do not scan, but fixing it without the spec would mean inventing a format rule.

proposals.title: docs: state in the README that vn-skills is an offline toolkit, not a payment gateway
proposals.body:
## Problem
People comparing VietQR MCP servers on Glama also see "AgentPay VN", a Python MCP server that collects real VietQR payments. The README does not say plainly what vn-skills does and does not do for payments. It builds, parses and validates payloads offline; it does not collect money, check transfers, or call bank or NAPAS APIs. Without that line, users may expect payment confirmation, or pass vn-skills over thinking it needs credentials.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Add a short "What it is / what it is not" paragraph near the top of `README.md` (after the layer table): offline, no accounts or API keys, builds/validates VietQR payloads and images, does **not** collect payments or confirm transfers; pair it with a payment gateway for that
- [ ] The same paragraph in Vietnamese in `README.vi.md`
- [ ] One line with the same message in `skills/vietqr/SKILL.md` ("Lỗi hay gặp" or an equivalent section) so agents do not promise payment confirmation
- [ ] Do not name or link competitors
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes; `pnpm format:check` passes
proposals.rationale: A clear position helps visitors from MCP directories choose vn-skills for what it does well (no credentials, works offline) instead of bouncing.

proposals.title: vietqr: collect sample MoMo, ZaloPay and VNPayQR payloads before adding parse support
proposals.body:
## Problem
`xuannghia/vietnam-qr-pay` (the upstream of `banks.json` and the top `vietqr` repo on GitHub) says it decodes VietQR, MoMo/ZaloPay multi-purpose QR and VNPayQR. `parseVietQR` handles NAPAS VietQR only. Users comparing the two will see the gap. The repository has no samples or cited spec for the wallet and VNPay formats, so they cannot be implemented without inventing format details.

## Checklist (maintainer)
- [ ] Collect anonymised sample payloads for MoMo, ZaloPay and VNPayQR (or a cited public spec for each)
- [ ] Run each through `node packages/cli/dist/index.js vietqr parse <payload>` and record the current output
- [ ] Decide the scope: recognise and label the scheme only, or decode its merchant fields as well
- [ ] Add the samples (with source/licence) to the issue, then split it into implementable issues with golden fixtures
proposals.rationale: [needs you] It is the main functional gap against the most popular adjacent library, but it needs real samples that are not in the repository.

proposals.title: vietqr: say when a parsed payload was lower-cased in transit instead of reporting a bare CRC mismatch
proposals.body:
## Problem

`parseVietQR` recomputes the CRC over the payload exactly as received (`packages/core/src/vietqr/parse.ts:44-46`). When a valid payload has been lower-cased by a chat app or a form, the CRC no longer matches and the warning makes the payload look corrupted:

```
parseVietQR(buildVietQR({...}).payload.toLowerCase())
=> ok: true, crcValid: false, warnings: [
  "CRC mismatch: payload has 8300, expected E6CC.",
  "Tag 38 GUID is \"a000000727\", not NAPAS A000000727."
]
```

The CRC hex digits are already compared case-insensitively (line 46). The mismatch happens because the CRC is computed over the lower-cased payload. A scanner would compute the CRC over the payload as given too, so `crcValid: false` is the correct result. The problem is that neither warning tells the user the real cause, which is that the case was changed, not the data.

## Proposal

- When `crcValid` is false, also compute `crc16CcittFalse` over the upper-cased prefix (`payload.slice(0, crcIndex + 4).toUpperCase()`). If that matches `crc.toUpperCase()`, replace the plain CRC mismatch warning with one that says the payload appears to have been lower-cased in transit and the CRC matches the upper-cased payload. It should also tell the user to use the original payload.
- If the tag 38 GUID differs from `A000000727` only by case, warn that the GUID is lower-cased instead of saying it is not NAPAS.
- Do not change `crcValid` semantics: it stays `false` for a payload whose CRC does not match as given.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A lower-cased payload built from an upper-case-only input (for example, no note or an upper-case note) gets the new lower-case warning and no "not NAPAS" GUID warning; `crcValid` is still `false`
- [ ] A payload with a genuinely wrong CRC still gets the existing `CRC mismatch: ...` warning
- [ ] A lower-cased payload whose original had a mixed-case note (the upper-case retry does not match) keeps the plain mismatch warning and gets no false hint
- [ ] Valid payloads parse exactly as before (existing tests unchanged)
- [ ] Golden case(s) added to `tests/golden/vietqr.json` in the existing case format
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: People paste payloads through tools that change case. Today the warning blames data corruption, so callers can't tell a mangled-but-recoverable code from a broken one.

proposals.title: vn-lunar: reject out-of-range day and month in parseDateInput
proposals.body:
## Problem

`parseDateInput` (`packages/core/src/lunar/index.ts:87-96`) only checks the shape of the string. `parseDateInput('0/1/2024')` returns `{ ok: true, day: 0, month: 1, year: 2024 }`, and inputs such as `32/1/2024`, `1/13/2024` and `2024-00-10` also pass. Callers re-validate later and return a generic `INVALID_DATE`, so the visible effect is a less precise error. Any caller that skips the second check would accept day 0. Non-padded forms (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`) are intentional and should stay accepted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `parseDateInput` returns `INVALID_DATE` when the month is outside 1-12 or the day is outside 1 to the number of days in that month (Gregorian, leap years included: `29/2/2024` ok, `29/2/2023` rejected)
- [ ] The error message names the bad part (e.g. `Day 0 is out of range for 01/2024`) and keeps the existing hint
- [ ] Non-padded inputs (`2024-2-3`, `1-2-2024`, `3/2/2024`) still parse
- [ ] Tests added to `tests/lunar.test.ts` for day 0, day 32, month 0, month 13, 31/4, 29/2 in leap and non-leap years, and the non-padded forms
- [ ] Existing CLI tests (`tests/cli.test.ts`) still pass; update expected messages only where the new message is more precise
- [ ] `pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm exec vitest run && pnpm format:check` pass
proposals.rationale: This is a small hardening fix. The helper is shared, so validating once here gives precise errors everywhere and removes the risk of a caller accepting day 0.

proposals.title: docs: add copy-paste MCP setup for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and Codex
proposals.body:
## Problem

`@vn-skills/mcp` is the most downloaded package (827/month), but the README's MCP section (`README.md`, "MCP server") shows only `claude mcp add` and one generic `mcpServers` JSON block. Not every client uses that shape. VS Code's `.vscode/mcp.json` uses a top-level `servers` key, and Codex reads TOML from `~/.codex/config.toml`. A user who pastes the generic JSON into one of those clients gets a server that never starts, and the README doesn't say where each file goes. `docs/quickstart.md` has the same gap.

This is the install-guide half of RM-003. The demo GIF half is tracked in #92.

## Proposal

Add a short "MCP client setup" subsection to `README.md` (and the same in `README.vi.md`) with one block per client:

- **Claude Code:** keep `claude mcp add vn-skills -- npx -y @vn-skills/mcp`
- **Claude Desktop:** `claude_desktop_config.json`, `{ "mcpServers": { "vn-skills": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Cursor:** `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global), same `mcpServers` shape
- **VS Code:** `.vscode/mcp.json`, `{ "servers": { "vn-skills": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"] } } }`
- **Codex:** `~/.codex/config.toml`:
  ```toml
  [mcp_servers.vn-skills]
  command = "npx"
  args = ["-y", "@vn-skills/mcp"]
  ```

Link each client to its official MCP documentation page so readers can check the file location. Keep the generic block for other clients. Mention that Node.js 22+ is required.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `README.md` has a block for each of the five clients above, each with a link to that client's MCP docs
- [ ] `README.vi.md` has the same content in Vietnamese
- [ ] `docs/quickstart.md` and `docs/quickstart.vi.md` link to the new section instead of duplicating it
- [ ] `tests/readme.test.ts` still passes (extend it if it checks the MCP section)
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` passes
proposals.rationale: MCP is the channel with the most downloads, and getting set up in a client is the step where people drop off. Snippets that work as pasted for each client turn downloads into working installs.

proposals.title: vn-einvoice: check whether Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP changes the rules or citations
proposals.body:
## Problem

`skills/vn-einvoice/SKILL.md`, `skills/vn-einvoice/references/schema.md`, `packages/core/src/einvoice/schema.ts` and the `vn_einvoice_validate` MCP tool description cite only Decree 123/2020/NĐ-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Published pages refer to a Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP that amends Decree 123/2020 on invoices and documents. Its text could not be read online: thuvienphapluat.vn returned 403 and the chinhphu.vn URL returned 404. Nothing in the repository says what it changes, so no code can change until the governing text is checked.

## Checklist

- [ ] Get the official text of Decree 70/2025/NĐ-CP (official gazette or chinhphu.vn) and record the URL and effective date in this issue
- [ ] Decide whether it changes anything the schema validates: required fields, invoice symbol or number format, buyer and seller fields, VAT handling or amount-in-words
- [ ] If nothing changes: open a follow-up to add the decree to the citations in `SKILL.md`, `references/schema.md`, `schema.ts` and the MCP description
- [ ] If rules change: open one follow-up issue per rule, each quoting the article and the expected input → output, so the change can be made with golden tests in `tests/golden/vn-einvoice.json`
proposals.rationale: [needs you] An e-invoice skill that cites outdated law loses trust fast. The legal reading needs a person, and the code work stays blocked until then.
